subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should maintainers adopt the shared guarded-write/CAS direction for exec approval stale writes, or sponsor a narrower allow-always-only fix for this issue?
rationale: The affected file is persisted command-approval state, and open/closed related PRs show competing fix shapes with unresolved security-review and proof gaps.

options.title: Adopt the shared guarded-write fix
options.body: Refresh the existing guarded-write direction on current main and require it to cover allow-always entries and usage metadata before merging.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow allow-always fix
options.body: Limit the repair to concurrent allow-always persistence while leaving broader usage-metadata writeback work on the linked security track.

options.title: Wait for the broader security PR
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader node stale-writeback fix is proven and either merged or rejected.

recommendation.title: Adopt the shared guarded-write fix
recommendation.body: Refresh the existing guarded-write direction on current main and require it to cover allow-always entries and usage metadata before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged and open exec approval work spans durable allow-always trust plus gateway/node approval freshness, making them the best available routing owner for the fix-shape decision.
